items.title: That 'Microsoft Support' Call Is a Scam — Hang Up Immediately
items.summary: Your phone rings. The caller says they are from Microsoft or Windows Support. They claim your computer has a virus, a security problem, or an expired license — and they need remote access to fix it. Sometimes they ask for a credit card or gift cards to "renew" your protection.

items.title: Two Critical Vulnerabilities Added to CISA Must-Patch List — Fortinet Firewalls and BeyondTrust Remote Support
items.summary: If your organization uses Fortinet firewalls or BeyondTrust Remote Support, apply the latest patches immediately at support.fortinet.com and beyondtrust.com/support — both fix flaws attackers are actively exploiting right now (CVE-2025-61624 and CVE-2026-102764).

items.title: Firefox 158 Adds Smart Window Form Filling and JPEG XL Support — Free Update at firefox.com
items.summary: Update Firefox at firefox.com or click Menu > Help > About Firefox — Smart Window now suggests form data from your open tabs and saved autofill, and JPEG XL images load faster with better quality than WebP.

items.title: Windows Sandbox Gives You a Free Disposable PC Inside Windows — Enable It at Windows Features
items.summary: Open Windows Features (type 'Windows Features' in Start), check Windows Sandbox, restart — you get a clean temporary desktop where anything you download, install, or break disappears when you close the window.

items.title: Rufus Makes a Bootable Windows USB in Minutes — Free at rufus.ie
items.summary: Download Rufus at rufus.ie, pick your Windows ISO and USB drive (8 GB minimum), click Start — a bootable Windows installer is ready in minutes, no command line required.

items.title: Windows 10 Support Ends October 14 — Free Upgrade to Windows 11 at Settings > Update
items.summary: After October 14, 2026, Windows 10 stops receiving security updates. Your computer will keep working, but it won't be safe to use online. Upgrade to Windows 11 for free at Settings > Windows Update > Check for Updates. Most PCs from 2018 or newer are eligible. Get the free upgrade at Settings > Windows Update

items.title: That CAPTCHA Asking You to Press Windows+R Is a Scam
items.summary: A fake CAPTCHA pops up and tells you to press the Windows key + R, paste something, and hit Enter. **Don't do it.** That "verification" is a trap — it pastes malicious code into Windows Run and executes it. Real CAPTCHAs never ask for keyboard commands. Ever.
